newsitem.title: USA: Florida plans to go ahead with tobacco trial.
newsitem.headline: Florida plans to go ahead with tobacco trial.

text.p: Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth on Tuesday the state was pushing ahead with preparations for a trial of its lawsuit against cigarette makers, denying negotiations with the tobacco industry to delay the case were under way.

"We're not going to delay our trial, no way. ...I spoke to my governor last night and I'm meeting him tomorrow and we're talking about trial strategy. We're ready to go to trial," Butterworth told Reuters at a meeting of state attorneys general in Wyoming.

The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that Florida and Texas were in discussions with the tobacco industry about postponing trials to recover billions of dollars in public funds spent on treating sick smokers.
Butterworth denied Florida was in negotiations with the industry on delaying its trial, scheduled to start August 4.
"As of today, we're not, we're absolutely not. I would anticipate there might be some overtures but as of right now, we're not at all in negotiations," he said.
While that was the situation at this time, Butterworth said, "By next week it might be a little different."

Suits filed by Mississippi, Florida and Texas are scheduled to go to trial before Congress is expected to take up a proposed $368.5 billion settlement reached last Friday between state attorneys general and the tobacco industry.
